fair_value_reason: The round-2 agent mean is $158.0 (160/171/134/168/157). Adjustments: agent_3 to ~$138, the midpoint between its methods-based $134 and a scenario mean of $141 that it fails to reconcile; agent_1 ~+$1 if FY29 is at least the lowest Zacks-implied value (~$13.0). That gives a corrected mean of ~$159. My own consensus-anchored build: NTM EPS ~$11.2 (10% below the consensus-implied $12.48, supported by both the 5-estimate Zacks FY29 and the $21 FY30 target) x 14.5-15x = $162-168; EV/EBITDA at ORCL's current ~8.5x on $77B (consensus NTM less 10%) less ~$140B net debt over ~3.13B shares = ~$164. I set $161 between the corrected agent mean and my build, ~12% above spot, on ~3.10-3.16B diluted shares and with operating leases excluded from net debt.
supervisor_summary: ORCL at $143.41 trades at 14.6x CY27 consensus EPS ($9.81), 33% below a verified 10-peer median of 21.65x, a discount the agents rightly hold through Oct-2027 given negative FCF through the FY27-28 peak-capex years, BBB-/Baa2-negative credit and OpenAI concentration. Round-2 fair values ($134-171, mean $158) moved almost exactly as my round-1 corrections predicted, which is partly anchoring. Independence survives only in the EPS haircut, where the consensus-implied FY29 (~$15.4 from 5 estimates) is backed by management's $21 FY30 target, so the 15% haircuts lean bearish. I corrected my own round-1 Jupiter claim: the force-majeure notice protects Oracle as tenant and the $18B loan is the landlord's, not an Oracle credit event. S&P's stable outlook is confirmed, but S&P ties it to positive FCF in 2028, which makes the June-2027 FY28 guide the key credit event. Reconciled fair value is $161 (~12% upside); I keep the agents' mean 12-month ladder (P(>=143) ~0.55) at low confidence, with the thesis break at $100.
key_drivers: Earnings path: CY27 consensus $9.81 (FY27 $8.14 / FY28 $11.00), so 14.6x at $143.41. Consensus-implied NTM at Oct-2027 is ~$12.5, with FY29 ~$15.4 on 5 Zacks estimates (implied range ~$13.0-17.6). Management's $21 FY30 target independently implies FY29 ~$15. The agents haircut NTM by 7-15%, and that judgment is the whole $134-171 spread.

Multiple: reconciled 10-peer CY27 median 21.65x. ORCL is 33% below it, and all agents hold 14-15x, justified on persistent negative FCF through FY28, BBB-/Baa2-negative credit, ~half of RPO with OpenAI and a ~23% non-GAAP/GAAP gap.

Funding and credit: net debt $88.2B now and ~$140B at Oct-2027 (without operating leases). $20-40B more debt or equity is due Jan-May 2027. S&P BBB- stable, but S&P says FCF must turn positive in 2028; Moody's Baa2 negative.

Delivery risk at the giga-sites: Oracle's Sep-24 force-majeure notice to Jupiter's developer (gas pipeline slipped to Feb-2027; Oracle says on schedule) and the Wisconsin transmission refiling. These are revenue-timing risks, not an Oracle loan problem.
Catalysts: October Investor Day (FCF date, AI-infrastructure margins), Q2 FY27 on Dec 14, Jan-May 2027 financing, and the June-2027 FY28 guide, which is the event S&P's trigger hangs on.
